stem: An electron is accelerated through a potential of 120 V. Find its de Broglie wavelength.
solution:
Given \(V = 120\) V.

We know that \(\lambda = \dfrac{1.228}{\sqrt{V}}\) nm using Eq. (14.7).

\(\therefore\ \lambda = \dfrac{1.228}{\sqrt{120}} = 0.112\) nm.

stem: A student, weighing 45 kg, is running with a speed of 8 km per hr on a foot path 2 m wide. A small car, weighing 1200 kg, is moving with a speed of 60 km per hr on a 20 m wide road. Calculate their de Broglie wavelengths.
solution:
Given
\(v_1 = 8\) km / hr \(= 8 \times 10^{3} / 3600\) m / s and \(m_1 = 45\) kg for the student,
\(v_2 = 60\) km / hr \(= 60 \times 10^{3} / 3600\) m / s and \(m_2 = 1200\) kg for the car,

momentum \(p_1 = 45 \times 8 \times 10^{3} / 3600 = 100\) kg m /s for the student and
momentum \(p_2 = 1200 \times 60 \times 10^{3} / 3600 = 20000\) kg m /s for the car.

The de Broglie wavelength
\(\lambda_1 = h/p_1 = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\) J s / 100 kg m /s
\(= 6.63 \times 10^{-36}\) m. for the student, and

de Broglie wavelength
\(\lambda_2 = h/p_2 = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\) J s / 20000 kg m /s
\(= 3.32 \times 10^{-38}\) m for the car.

stem: Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of an electron moving with kinetic energy of 100 eV passing through a circular hole of diameter 2 \(\mathring{A}\).
solution:
Given
\(E_K = 100\) eV \(= 100 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\) J.

The speed of the electron is given by the relation \(\dfrac{1}{2} m v^2 = 100 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\) J.

\(\therefore\ v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 100 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\ \text{J}}{9.11 \times 10^{-31}\ \text{kg}}}\)
\(= 5.927 \times 10^{6}\) m/s and

momentum \(p = 9.11 \times 10^{-31}\) kg \(\times\ 0.593 \times 10^{7}\) m/s \(= 5.40 \times 10^{-24}\) kg m/s

\(\therefore\) the de Broglie wavelength \(\lambda = h/p\)
\(= 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\) J s / \(5.40 \times 10^{-24}\) kg m/s
\(= 1.23 \times 10^{-10}\) m \(= 1.228\, \mathring{A}\).
